newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CMB sees 1997 profit from Saga stake.
newsitem.headline: CMB sees 1997 profit from Saga stake.

text.p: Belgian diversified shipper CMB said on Wednesday it expected a profit from its investment in French ports company Saga already in 1997.
CMB and the French Bollore group bought 80 percent of then ailing Saga late last year.
Chief executive officer Marc Saverys told the annual shareholders meeting in Antwerp that Saga's two main problem areas in the French ports of Marseille and Le Havre had been solved.
"We expect a small positive contribution from Saga... by the end of this year all negative elements in Saga should be solved or sold."

He told Reuters Saga had been close to bankruptcy because of its 50 percent stake in a terminal in Le Havre and a company in Marseille. CMB managed to sell 50 percent of the TN terminal stake to Bollore. The Marseille company went bankrupt, but CMB was able to recover large provisions for possible legal action resulting from the Marseille company's bankruptcy.
"Now the two problem children, who almost bankrupted Saga, have been removed," he said.
CMB now had a 30 percent direct stake in Saga.

Finance director Ludwig Criel said CMB and Bollore had paid about 220 million French francs for their stake in Saga. The partners planned a 60 million French franc capital increase in the near future.
